A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoQuIR and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–B. Reformatting, renumbering, and removal of v2's checklist do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 23 retrievers, quality-aware fine-tuning experiments, downstream code-generation results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original retrieval and downstream experiments and adds a human evaluation of 400 generated query summaries.

M1.justification: The contrastive training approach, Repllama backbones, synthetic security/API-migration pairs, and MS MARCO training remain. Appendix B.6 retains the same LoRA configuration; compressed descriptions do not establish an actual method change.

E1.justification: The seven retrieval datasets, eleven languages, four quality dimensions, training sources, and downstream security/API-use scenarios are retained. The new summary audit examines existing datasets rather than extending benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same 23 retrievers. Corresponding instruction-sensitivity, fine-tuning, and downstream comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds an evaluation protocol: three expert co-authors independently rate 100 randomly sampled summaries from each of Defects4J, CVEFixes, SQLR2, and DepreAPI using five-point correctness and quality-neutrality scales. Existing retrieval and downstream settings remain as stated.

E4.justification: V2's Appendix B.3 only documented summarization prompts and leakage-prevention instructions; v3 adds empirical human validation of summary faithfulness and quality-neutrality. Existing language, instruction-sensitivity, correlation, and downstream analyses remain, including renumbered appendix figures.

E5.justification: V3 introduces inter-annotator agreement reporting using Fleiss' kappa for the summary audit. Both versions report three downstream generation runs; no increase in runs or expanded retrieval uncertainty reporting is established.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 contain identical scores. V3 adds summary correctness averages of 4.5–4.7, compliance averages of 4.4–4.6, and kappa of 0.72. Figure 4 also revises Repllama-3b-quality's DepreAPI bars from approximately 61% to 66% nDCG@10 and 52% to 57% MRR, without explaining the revisions or reporting changed conditions.

T1.justification: The PPA/MRS equations and existing mathematical arguments remain unchanged. However, Table 2 newly asserts a 50% random-ranking baseline for both nDCG@10 and MRR, adding an unsupported mathematical reference assumption without a derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the four-dimension CoQuIR benchmark, evaluation of 23 retrievers, two quality-aware metrics, and contrastive training that benefits retrieval and downstream generation.

C2.justification: V3 adds limitations concerning summary inaccuracies, sparse-language robustness, and missing comparisons with static filtering or unit testing, positioning these techniques as complementary. It removes speculation about Voyage's training objectives and the blanket interpretation that larger instruction-tuned models have stronger quality-awareness.

D1.justification: V3 adds approximately ten hours of training on two A100 40GB GPUs and human-rating instructions. It omits the project GitHub link and v2's stated requirement that selected CodeNet training problems span at least four languages. The dataset link and detailed training hyperparameters remain; code unavailability is not established.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on retrieval poisoning, testing/static-analysis costs, and software-quality standards, while dropping Xiong et al.'s dense-retrieval citation. These additions broaden motivation and positioning without replacing the central distinction from relevance-focused retrieval benchmarks.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting compresses the abstract and methodological descriptions, expands the introduction, and integrates the former Section 4.3 analyses into Section 4.2. V3 also renames sections, adds separate acknowledgment and ethics text, rewrites limitations, updates affiliations, and removes the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout, reformats and relocates tables and appendix figures, and redraws Figures 1, 3b, and 4. Figure 2 gains explanatory strips, Table 2 gains blue/pink shading, and a new human-evaluation rubric becomes Table 8; the existing synthesis prompts move to Table 9.

improvement.justification: The 400-summary audit and hardware disclosure strengthen validation and reproducibility. However, v3 introduces an unsupported 50% random baseline for nDCG/MRR in Table 2, an incorrect left/right explanation in Figure 2, and unexplained DepreAPI score revisions in Figure 4. These benefits and reporting problems leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
